title: A Selection of Shen Gua’s Writings in Translation, Appendix 3, item 307
lineage: A late-eleventh-century narrative in a modern scholarly translation, with its ancient Chinese text. Only item 307, notes 67–72, and editorial framing were inspected. The three nodes unpack one reported configuration, not three independent inventions. No surviving Bi Sheng types or production quantities inspected. Note 69 records disagreement over clay composition.

passages.locator: Printed pp. 22–23, item 307, opening; web extraction lines 654–675
passages.note: Shen dates Bi Sheng’s practice to that reign; types are individually carved and fired, then assembled on a coated iron plate within a frame.
Individually carved types are hardened by fire.

passages.locator: Printed p. 23, item 307, first paragraph, assembly sentences
passages.quote: puts an iron frame on top
passages.note: Types are composed closely on a coated iron plate, then heated and leveled.
Two boards alternate composition and printing.

passages.quote: the types will easily fall out
passages.note: Reheating releases the types; the following sentence says Shen’s family obtained them after Bi’s death.
